newsitem.title: USA: TV ready to revise parental ratings, lawmakers say.
newsitem.headline: TV ready to revise parental ratings, lawmakers say.

text.p: The television industry has accepted that it must swiftly revise the age-based ratings system in a way that satisfies parents groups or else face likely government regulation, lawmakers said Wednesday.

Cable, broadcast and Hollywood branches of the industry agreed in a meeting with lawmakers Wednesday to work over the next two weeks with prominent family-oriented organisations to revise the system, lawmakers said.
The age-based rating system was designed a year ago but has not satisfied advocacy groups or lawmakers.
The industry did not specifically agree to add the labels "S" for sexual content, "V" for violence, and "L" for adult language, but those codes were not rejected out of hand.
"They did not make that commitment," Sen. John McCain, the Arizona Republican who chairs the Commerce Committee, told reporters. "They didn't say no, either."
McCain, joined by Republican and Democratic colleagues from the House and Senate, said the meeting with the industry went well. McCain said he expects significant progress within two weeks.
The industry in that time will consult with leading parent groups, including the Parent Teachers Association (PTA), and a leading pediatricians group, the lawmakers said.

They said the industry clearly got the message that families expected -- and lawmakers agreed -- that in order to be useful to parents the ratings must be more precise, give more information and be uniform from one channel to another.

If the negotiations failed, at least two Senate proposals to require a different rating systems are in the wings, and would probably pass easily. "It would become an irresistable political force in the United States," said Representative Ed Markey, a Massachusetts Democrat.
